Indian Standard
SPECIFICATIONS FOR TEST FILMS FOR 35 mm MOTION-PICTURE SOUND REPRODUCERS, PHOTOGRAPHIC TYPE
0. FOREWORD

0.1 These Indian Standards were adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 17 April 1972, after the drufts finalized by the Cinematographic Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Blectrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 Test films are important tools in attaining and assuring acceptable and uniform performance for motion-picture equipment. This series ofstandards is intended to cover the following test films: a) Buzz-track b) 1000 test film, and signal level test film,

Hz balancing

c) Sound-focusing d) Scanning-beam

test film, and uniformity test film.

0.3 Care should-be taken by users of these test films that the characteristics of the films are not altered by shrinkage due to incorrect storage conditions. Recommendations on the storage of films and determination of shrinkage of film stock are given in Appendix A and Appendix B respectively. 0.4 In preparing these standards, p~rhlishrd following standards Institute, USA: i,y assistance has been derived the Amrviran National test films film for 35 mm motionsound from the Standard

uniformity test sound reproducers film

for 35 mm

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of these standards is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in these standards.

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR SCANNING BEAM UNIFORMITY TEST FILM
UDC
1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements determining the uniformity of scanning motion-picture sound reproducers. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, ( Part XXXIV )-1972* shall apply. 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 TrpeThe test film shall be a print from an original negative. the definitions given in IS : 1885 for a film that may be used for beam illumination in 35 mm

771.531,351 : 620*115*8

3.2 Dimensions - The dimensions and location of the sound record shall be as specified in Fig. 1. In any one test film, the width of the sound track shall not vary more than 5 percent of the average sound record width. 3.3 Position - The track shall move uniformly 2.06 mm from one edge of the scanned area to the other; as shown in Fig. 1. The recording method shall be such as to expose only the indicated track area within the reproducer scanning width. 3.4 Rtcodlng - The sound record shall be a square-wave recording having pulse rise-and-fail times of less than 30 microseconds. At a film velocity of 45.7 cm/s, the pulse-repetition rate shall be 1 000 f 20 pulses per second. 3.3 Density -The exposed areas of the film shall have a minimum diffuse density of 2.0 above base density measured in an area of normal sound record width ( 1.524 mm ) of half-track exposed for the purpose outside the snaketrack region. Variations from avcragc shall not exceed 0.1. The unexposed areas shall have a maximum density of 0.10 above base density with variations from average of not more than 0.015. l Elcctrotechnical vocabulary: Part XXXIV Cinematography ( w&print ). 9

4.1 Before the test film described in this standard ed that correct placement of the scanning beam of a buzz-track test film (see IS : 6561-19727 ).

The uniformity of scanning-beam illumination may be measured by means of a sound level meter connected to the output of the sound projector amplifier. The illumination of the scanning-bran1 should be adjusted according to the instructions furnished by the mantJacturer and the variation of the output as registered on the sound level nletcr should be observed. The illumination is considered satisfactorily uni!`brm when the output reading, as -measured by the metrr is within f 14 dl% across the entire scanning slit. The test film made in accordance \vith this standard is not intended for positioning of the scanning beam. AFPENDIX
( Clause 0.3 )
RECOMMENDATIONS ON STORAGE ACETATE FILMS A-l. CONTAINERS

A
OF CELLULOSE

A-l.1 The film should be kept, preferably wound, in cylindrical containers provided with a dutt-tight lid and made of material which will have no deleterious effect on ihe film. A-2. METHOD A-2.1 The
diameter the film.

OF STORAGE

innermost layer of the roil of film should not be wound to a smaller than 3 cm, and it is desirable to use a suitable core for

A-2.2 The film should be wound carefully and no attempt made to tighten the roll by pulling on one end of the strip; this would damage the film. A-2.3 The outer layer of the film should be held in position by a paper strip or other means, such as an outer wrapping of waste film secured with adhesive tape. Rubber bands should not be used to secure the film, if stored in rolls. A-3.

STORAGE

CONDITIONS

A-3.1 The

containers holding the film should be stored in an atmosphere which should have a relative humidity of not less than 30 percent ( to avoid brittleness ) nor more than 75 percent ( to avoid exudation of plasticizer and the sticking of the film )* A-3.2 The temperature should not be less than 0�C nor more than #)OC.

APPENDIX ( CZause 0.3 )
DETERMINATION El.
for a 6.4 50

B
OF FILM STOCK

OF SHRINKAGE

At least 20 strips of film approximately 80 cm in length shall be cut measurement of shrinkage. After normal development and drying at temperature not exceeding 27"C, the strips shall be placed at least mm apart in racks and kept for 7 days in an oven maintained at f 2�C and a relative humidity of 20 percent.

B-2. The strips shall then be removed, reconditioned thoroughly to 50 percent relative humidity at 20 f ~2�C and the shrinkage measured by a suitable method. B-3. The percent shrinkage shall then be calculated on the deviation from the nominal dimension for the length consecutive perforation intervals given in IS : 6084-I 971*. basis of of 100
